what: In-repo extract of the two claims in docs/tool-findings.md whose inputs are neither committed nor durable: the per-iteration violation series and the byte-identical route-pass DRC report pair. The inputs live only in a gitignored .klt/ directory and in a batch bucket whose objects expire (~2026-12-18; operator holds a copy, see issue #808 comment 6967987133). Committing the extract resolves #1006's 'decide' item: a number without its inputs is a claim, so the claim travels with the repo and the inputs stay bound by sha256.

per_iteration_violation_series.claim: The detailed-route iteration series ended stuck at 24: 2250 at iteration 0, 24 from iteration 4 onward, with brief transient bumps (32 at 17, 27 at 25, 25 at 41/49/57), and 24 at the final iteration 60 -- the router did not clear them.
per_iteration_violation_series.note: Keys are present only for iterations the metrics recorded; the gaps (7-9, 12-14, 22, 29, 36, 47-48, 54-56) are absent keys, not zeros, and were not interpolated. A second series under the route__ prefix agrees (43 points, same shape, same final 24).

route_pass_pair_byte_identical.claim: klayout-tools#2089's doubling is not seen at klt 0.9.0: the build emits a distinct report path per detailed_route call (ladder_dp_route_pass_0_drc.rpt from the first call, ladder_dp_route_drc.rpt from the last) and the two files are byte-identical with 24 records each, because antenna repair found 0 violations and the second pass changed nothing. The committed 0.5.0 baseline is 46 records / 23 distinct sites, every one doubled -- the defect re-used one path; this build's mechanism is structurally absent.

headline_counts.note: Each headline key occurs exactly once in the raw metrics file (no literal duplicate keys), so what json.loads sees and what the file says agree.
